# MaterialCraft parity fixes

This record follows the [SBS root-node inventory](sbs-root-nodes.md). The first pass classified 166 of 546 roots as Parity and 380 as Too hard. The inventory gives the current status of each root.

## Comparison method and provenance

MaterialCraft's clean-room evaluator is written independently in Rust. The directional-noise comparisons use configured SBS graphs and original procedural test patterns. Each application renders the specified graph, size, seed, parameters and output format. For bitmaps, a pixel counts as exact when its raw channel values match at the reported precision. Maximum error is the largest absolute channel difference, in storage levels for integer formats. Value graphs are compared at their declared type. The tables identify original renders, saved-file reopens and processor counts where those differ.

An intermediate image is a graph node's output. Some tests expose that node as an additional graph output. An instrumented MaterialCraft build can record individual additions, cache hits and work counts in its own evaluator. The reported reference values come from rendered outputs or the exposed properties named in the test. The draw-order tests compare candidate addition sequences with marker pixels from repeated renders. Several sequences can produce the same stored value. The [paired-square regression](../crates/nodes/src/pattern/tests/paired_batches.rs) constructs the pattern graph and generates its input image in Rust.

The project records the source and license of bundled graphs and resources in its [asset attribution](../ATTRIBUTION.md).

## Initial fixes

- **2026-11-13 — SBS swizzle defaults (orientation corrected):** Removed the importer's zero-channel overrides for omitted two-, three-, and four-component float/integer swizzle settings. Imports now use the existing identity-channel defaults from the function catalog. The first affected node, `3d_gradient.sbs/3d_linear_gradient`, previously repeated X instead of preserving XYZ, producing a horizontal gradient instead of the reference diagonal gradient. Compared both point-position modes with generated position maps at 256 and 512 pixels. Remaining float differences are recorded below; full node parity is not claimed.
- **2026-11-13 — Filtered function sampling (integer probes exact):** Added cooked-image storage precision to function samplers. Bilinear reads use eight fractional bits for filter weights. Normalized integer textures return 16-bit filtered values (including 8-bit sources); floating-point textures retain floating-point values. Input bridges retain the integer/floating-point distinction, and cache keys include it. Direct reference measurements on a generated position ramp showed a 16-bit half-step rounding to the next integer, explaining the remaining UV-gradient offset after the swizzle fix. All six measured integer-source sampler cases match all 65,536 float pixels exactly. Two of three floating-source cases are exact; one differs by 5.96e-8. Full-gradient rounding differences remain below.

- **2026-11-13 - SBS format inheritance (measured improvement):** Read and save the declared native graph output format instead of dropping it. An omitted format retains inheritance; comparison cases explicitly align the parent format to the reference preview (eight bits). Pixel Processors with omitted format settings now inherit the parent format instead of an image input format. This was exposed by `3d_perlin_noise.sbs/3D_perlin_noise`: the reference processor produces eight-bit output even though its position and lookup inputs are sixteen-bit. The Perlin comparison improved from 63,461/65,536 to 65,533/65,536 matching 8-bit pixels at 256 pixels; three additional 128-pixel cases match exactly. All four native format codes are serialized explicitly on save.

- **2026-11-13 - Floored floating-point modulo (randomized jump flood exact):** Replaced signed remainder with `a - b * floor(a / b)`. Direct reference probes confirm all sign combinations, including `-1 mod 4 = 3`, `1 mod -4 = -3`, and `-5.5 mod 4 = 2.5`. This corrects negative coordinate wrapping used by 3D texture jump flood. Both randomized 128x128 jump-flood cases (iterations 0 and 1, with disabled seed points) now match all 32,768 RGBA pixels exactly; the three ramp cases also match. All 131,072 RGBA pixels across five cases are exact.

- **2026-11-13 - Bound input storage and resizing:** Bound image inputs now store their declared output precision instead of passing unconverted floats downstream. Resizing clamps resource edges and proceeds through factor-two stored levels. A generated HDR 16x8 ramp resized to 32x32 now matches every RGBA8 input-bridge pixel; previously its center sample was 1.0 instead of 0.9843137. A randomized 64x32-to-32x32 downsample also matches every pixel. Three harder randomized multilevel cases retain single-level differences (4/1,024, 51/4,096, and 6/256 pixels), so general resampling parity is not claimed.

- **2026-11-13 - Half-float output storage:** Sixteen-bit floating-point outputs now convert to half precision, truncate toward zero, and saturate at +/-65,504. Previously they retained full 32-bit precision. All 2,304 pixels across nine direct reference probes match exactly, covering positive/negative values, rounding boundaries, a subnormal, maximum finite values, and positive/negative overflow. Uses the existing workspace half dependency (MIT OR Apache-2.0).

- **2026-11-13 - Volume-light function expansion:** Raised the bounded expanded-function allowance from 65,536 to 131,072 nodes after measuring the legitimate volume-light processor at 72,973 nodes and four call levels. The individual 4,096-node graph limit, 16-level call limit, cycle checks, and execution budget remain enforced. Error messages now report the actual limits. Three previously rejected light-render cases cook successfully; 760/768 RGBA16F pixels match, with the remaining differences recorded below.

- **2026-11-13 - Omitted function sampler settings:** Corrected Sample Color/Gray defaults to image zero with nearest filtering. Explicit bilinear settings are retained. Both original omitted-setting probes match all 32,768 float pixels. This removes the shifted edges of the 3D volume mask: default outputs at 128x128 and 256x256 and the changed-scale 128x128 case now match every sixteen-bit pixel.

- **2026-11-13 - Finite results after undefined pixel intermediates:** Pixel Processor arithmetic and vector operations now retain IEEE intermediate values so a later min/max can clamp division by zero to a finite result. Non-finite final pixels still return an actionable error. Parameter and pattern functions are checked at their public evaluation boundary. Four original clamp probes (positive infinity, negative infinity, NaN, and finite division) match all 1,024 float pixels. Cylinder-mask cases previously failed at the exact sampled center; they now cook successfully, with the residual conversion differences recorded below.

- **2026-11-13 - Independent transform wrapping:** Transformation 2D now uses horizontal and vertical tiling flags independently, with matching per-axis image sampling. Previously a horizontal-only panorama lost horizontal wrapping because the two flags collapsed to one boolean. All 131,072 RGBA8 pixels across eight original transform probes match exactly, covering both one-axis modes, positive/negative offsets, matte edges, and varying alpha. The panorama helper improves, but its remaining minification/filtering differences are recorded below.

- **2026-11-13 - Blend alpha, copy, and HDR:** Corrected the Switch stages used by Copy and other graphs to interpolate RGBA without weighting foreground alpha twice. Copy, Add, and other color modes now combine alpha coverage when alpha blending is enabled; disabling alpha blending preserves background alpha while RGB still uses foreground coverage. Integer clipping happens after opacity; floating-point formats retain HDR output. All 19 independent blend graphs are being measured with opaque/varying-alpha inputs, masks, opacity changes, and alpha-channel blending disabled. Direct Add/Copy HDR cases match all 512 RGBA32F pixels. Fourteen blend graphs now match every pixel across four RGBA8 cases each (1,605,632 pixels); Add and Copy also pass their HDR cases. The blend properties label and all four alpha-interpretation menu entries were checked visually in the running native app.

- **2026-11-13 - Function validation at result boundaries:** Original clamp probes confirm that node-parameter and pattern functions also accept undefined intermediates when later operations produce a finite result. Deferred those intermediate checks and retained explicit final-result validation. The original four node-parameter and four pattern probes match all 2,048 output pixels; unclamped pixel and node-parameter probes still return clear non-finite-output errors. Ordered NaN comparisons now return false, as measured for all four relational operators. All 5,120 float pixels across the twenty NaN/infinity/finite/zero comparison cases match exactly.

- **2026-11-13 - Grayscale default precision:** Default grayscale rendering now uses one third per RGB channel instead of 0.333, which previously darkened equal channels. This makes Add Sub exact in all four RGBA8 cases and reduces Luminosity from 8,407 mismatching pixels to two. Original float probes establish the fused red/green/blue/alpha dot-product order; all 65,536 float pixels across default, custom, sum-three, and zero-weight cases match exactly. Explicit channel weights retain their authored values.

- **2026-11-13 - Declared image types:** Imported single-output filters with an omitted color-mode parameter now retain the color/grayscale type declared in their SBS output. The bevel debug helper previously dropped RGBA coordinate data into a grayscale pattern buffer. It now cooks in the correct four-channel format. Explicit settings and functions remain authoritative.

- **2026-11-13 - Pattern alpha and empty backgrounds:** Color pattern maps now start transparent. Scalar luminosity/opacity affects alpha as well as RGB, without multiplying RGB twice. Eight original empty/scalar/RGBA/HDR pattern probes match all 2,048 RGBA32F pixels across additive and both maximum blend modes. The existing White Noise result still matches every one of its 65,536 sixteen-bit pixels.

- **2026-11-13 - Color resources on grayscale input pins:** Bound color images now use equal RGB weights at grayscale input bridges. The general display-luminance utility retains its documented behavior. All nine eight-bit grayscale switch cases match 294,912 pixels; two additional float switch cases match all 32,768 pixels exactly, including varying source alpha. Previously only about one percent of the eight-bit pixels matched.

- **2026-11-13 - Transform matrix layout:** Transformation 2D now reads consecutive columns in the stored matrix and uses the same convention when selecting nearest mip levels. Previously rotations ran in the opposite direction and shears used the wrong axis. All 131,072 RGBA8 pixels across eight original shear/quarter-turn/diagonal/offset probes match exactly. Both unscaled rotated-checker cases also become exact. Scaled filtering remains open.

- **2026-11-13 - Legacy blend alpha interpretation:** Imported and implemented the older source-alpha/ignore-alpha/straight/premultiplied setting instead of dropping it. Direct runtime enum inspection confirms the four modes. Original Copy/Add/Max probes cover opacity changes, alpha-channel blending disabled, and 128x128/256x256 outputs. Ignore-alpha controls RGB weighting independently of output coverage; straight compositing includes background coverage, while premultiplied Copy consumes premultiplied foreground RGB. All four Clamp cases now match every one of 114,688 RGBA8 pixels. All 48 direct Copy/Add/Max cases cook; seven of the twelve mode/interpretation combinations match all 114,688 pixels, while the other five retain 11 one-level differences in total. Straight HDR output remains unclipped; its float differences reach 3.577e-7.

- **2026-11-13 - Integer options read as Boolean:** A legacy color-temperature function reads an integer option through Get Boolean. Original probes confirm that zero is false and positive/negative integers, including the minimum 32-bit value, are true. Added that conversion for user integer/enum variables while retaining strict system-variable and other getter types. All 1,280 float pixels across the five direct cases match exactly. Color temperature now cooks in all four cases; only two one-level pixels remain different.

- **2026-11-13 - Internal images down to one texel:** Removed the evaluator's 16-pixel floor for internal node sizes. The graph editor retains its own graph-size setting range. Internal reductions and lookup images can now use their declared 1..8,192 dimensions. Direct 1x1, 2x4, and 8x2 RGBA32F probes match all 25 pixels. The curvature helper's four small cases now use the correct 2x2/4x4 outputs and match all 28 pixels; two larger nonconstant cases also match all 16,640 RGBA32F pixels. All 655,360 pixels across 22 earlier Perlin-fractal, simplex, jump-flood, angle-vector, checker, and live White Noise cases still match exactly.

- **2026-11-13 - Integer Pixel Processor storage:** Original eight- and sixteen-bit probes confirm NaN converts to black, positive infinity to white, and negative infinity to black. Deferred Pixel Processor finite checks to integer storage for those formats, retaining final floating-point output validation. Integer storage now saturates infinities instead of treating every non-finite value as zero. All 2,560 pixels across ten direct integer probes match exactly. The zero-softness color mask and radial gradient now cook in all four cases each, with only one-level residual differences. Unclamped floating-point Pixel Processors still return a non-finite-output error.

- **2026-11-13 - Swizzle padding:** Vector swizzles now read components outside the source dimension as zero, including scalar inputs. Arithmetic scalar broadcasting remains available to arithmetic operations. All 1,792 RGBA32F pixels across seven original float/integer probes match exactly. Histogram computation now cooks in all four cases; its remaining numerical differences are recorded below.

- **2026-11-13 - Grayscale resources on color input pins:** Color input bridges now promote grayscale resources to RGB with opaque alpha. Both original 128x128 and 256x256 probes match all 81,920 RGBA8 pixels exactly.

- **2026-11-13 - Unassigned user variables:** Numeric user-variable getters now return typed zero, and Boolean getters return false, before the first assignment. Previously they raised an undefined-variable error. Original probes add a nonzero value after each getter so a failed black render cannot look like a match. All 2,304 float/RGBA32F pixels across Boolean, integer1..4, and float1..4 cases match exactly. System-variable availability, existing-variable type checks, and string errors remain strict. All four affected Voronoi graphs now cook across four 16x16/32x32 cases each; numerical differences remain. The 128x128 fractal case also cooks and matches 15,457/16,384 pixels. The previously failing matte and shadow helper now cook in all four cases each, with remaining output differences.

- **2026-11-13 - RGBA results in grayscale Pixel Processors:** Grayscale processors now convert a four-component result with equal RGB weights instead of taking red alone. Alpha does not contribute. Original HDR and negative-value probes establish the fused green/red/blue accumulation order; all 9,216 LUM32F pixels across 36 cases match exactly. The three affected grayscale rendering templates now match all 344,064 LUM8 pixels across twelve cases; the color template retains all 114,688 exact RGBA8 pixels.

- **2026-11-13 - Float-to-integer conversion:** Finite scalar and vector conversion now rounds down, correcting negative coordinates that previously truncated toward zero. All 6,144 float/RGBA32F pixels and 18 typed integer outputs match the original reference probes. Non-finite and out-of-range integer conversions retain actionable errors; parity for those inputs is not claimed. The 22 previously verified cases still match all 655,360 pixels after this change.

- **2026-11-13 - Unconnected output images:** Unconnected output bridges now produce transparent RGBA instead of grayscale. The importer separately retains each output's declared image type so saving an unconnected output preserves the graph interface. Both material templates match all 1,179,648 RGBA8 pixels across six recorded cases. All 2,560 direct grayscale/color declaration probe pixels also match, and both declared image types survive save/reload.

### Seeded placement in the remaining Directional Noise 3 rectangles

The shared FX-Map evaluator now binds pure grayscale frame offsets, rotations and luminosities for eligible drawing quadrants. It evaluates each random stream at its original property and charges the arithmetic that runs. A drawing function with unsupported instructions or a mutable input uses the ordinary evaluator. The visit, property-work, raster and cache ceilings still apply. The 64 × 16 and 64 × 32 settings previously exhausted the property budget in F32. Their sixteen and eighteen emitted trees have 6,275,400 and 6,785,426 distinct node, depth and seed combinations. ### An additive wave at a 16-bit storage boundary

Use the 64 × 16 Directional Noise 3 setting with seed 42 and the 64 × 32 setting with seed 195031. For each selected format, collect four original renders on one processor and four on eight, then reopen an ordinary save on each processor count. At 64 × 32 every local U16 and F32 word occurs in at least one of the ten corresponding reference returns. At 64 × 16 in F32, one local value falls outside all ten returns. At (19, 14) MaterialCraft gives .5435512066 and all ten reference returns give .5435265899. [Full settings and file routes](#seeded-placement-in-the-remaining-directional-noise-3-rectangles)

Add outputs to the three wave patterns and the two blends in the configured 64 × 16 graph. Keep the original normalization and storage. The first two patterns match all 16 and 64 U16 pixels, and the first blend matches all 1,024. The third pattern gives 20,789 at (19, 14) in MaterialCraft and 20,788 in both reference captures. The second blend carries that difference to 39,704 and 39,703. The final Levels output retains the measured F32 difference.

Set only the third pattern to F32 and read the draws before integer storage. Compare the original additive setting with maximum blending on its wave quadrants. Both processor counts give the following whole-image comparisons.

| Output at 64 × 16 | Additive exact · max | Maximum blending exact · max |
|---|---:|---:|
| Third pattern | 326/1,024 · 1.78813934e-07 | 1,024/1,024 · 0 |
| Following blend | 627/1,024 · 1.78813934e-07 | 1,024/1,024 · 0 |
| Levels | 637/1,024 · 3.57627869e-07 | 1,024/1,024 · 0 |

At (19, 14) the additive pattern gives .317213088274 in MaterialCraft and .317212998867 in both reference captures. Flooring these values at 20 fractional bits gives 332,622 and 332,621. Converting each application’s F32 values through the normalized U16 store reproduces its own **1,024/1,024** original U16 words. The difference is already present in the floating-point sum.

Connect the third pattern directly to the output, keeping its graph settings, and cap only the outer iteration count. Both reference processor counts agree on every pixel of each reduced case.

| Emitted trees | F32 exact · maximum |
|---:|---:|
| 1 | 959/1,024 · 1.1920929e-07 |
| 2 | 952/1,024 · 1.1920929e-07 |
| 4 | 911/1,024 · 2.68220901e-07 |
| 8 | 764/1,024 · 1.78813934e-07 |

Keep one emitted tree and follow quadrant slots 1, 0, 1 to the next fork. All four child subtrees measured individually match 1,024/1,024. All sixteen grandchildren also match individually, **16,384/16,384**. With two child slots connected, the six pairs together give **6,137/6,144 · 3.7252903e-09**. With three connected, the four combinations give **4,089/4,096 · 7.4505806e-09**. Both processor counts give these results.

Replaying each child’s measured contributions as a contiguous group fails to reproduce the reference in four of six pairs and three of four triples, even after trying every child order. Grouping the individual MaterialCraft stamp contributions one level deeper gives six candidate orders that each reproduce all 16 affected positions in every pair. These settings narrow the draw-order discrepancy. Directional Noise 3 remains in progress.

### Floating-point modulo at a rounded period

A runtime float modulo can round to the divisor when a very small input has the opposite sign. The reference returns zero at that endpoint. Constant expressions retain the rounded divisor. MaterialCraft now makes that distinction in the shared floating-point operator. The FX-Map drawing evaluator uses the same operator. The original graphs and their live functions supply all parameters. [Quadrant-path measurements](#locating-individual-waves-in-directional-noise-2-v2)

Use a grayscale square over black with unit opacity and zero roughness. Drive its luminosity with two exposed scalar values passed to modulo. Repeat in a grayscale Uniform and a grayscale Pixel Processor. Read stored F32 at 16². For each divisor 1, −1, .125, 3 and −1.5, let g be the difference between its magnitude and the next smaller positive F32. Multiply g by the divisor sign and each of −1.125, −1, −.75, −.5, −.25, .25, .5, .75 and 1.25. Also test the divisor itself and the values immediately to either side. The last six signed operand pairs are (.3125000298023224, 1), (−.3125000298023224, 1), (.2, .3), (−.2, .3), (−1.25, 3) and (1.25, −3). Use seeds 42, 43 and 44 cyclically.

| Original independent F32 control | Before · one · max | Current · one · max | Current · eight · max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Drawing property | 14,336/16,896 · 3 | 16,896/16,896 · 0 | 16,896/16,896 · 0 |
| Uniform property | 14,336/16,896 · 3 | 16,896/16,896 · 0 | 16,896/16,896 · 0 |
| Pixel Processor | 14,336/16,896 · 3 | 16,896/16,896 · 0 | 16,896/16,896 · 0 |

The nine literal controls give 2,304/2,304 · 0 on both processor counts. With divisor 1, literal −2⁻²⁵ gives 1 and a live input of the same value gives zero. A live input of −.75 × 2⁻²⁴ gives the predecessor of 1. Mirror the signs for a negative divisor. In a separate Pixel Processor select the input or its negative using the horizontal pixel coordinate. Thirteen split images improve from 2,304/3,328 · 3 to **3,328/3,328 · 0** on one processor. The same current result holds on eight.

The 36 earlier seeded offset settings and 36 ordinary reopens each retain 15,360/15,360 pixels on one and eight processors, maximum zero. [Seeded modulo controls and four storage formats](#floored-modulo-in-seeded-drawing-properties)

### An unfinished draw batch across repeated quadrant pairs

When an outer Iterate emits multiple two-child quadrant trees, each first child can draw before the shared path and the second child from all repetitions. The continuation contains the shared path and the last connected child of each tree. MaterialCraft counts its physical tile copies, including copies of draws that miss the pixel grid. The measured order applies while this continuation holds fewer than 5,460 copies. [Single-tree draw order and procedural construction](#drawing-a-shared-quadrant-path-with-its-last-child)

### Drawing a shared quadrant path with its last child

In a grayscale additive FX-Map, follow a single path to its first fork with six more quadrant subdivisions to the deepest leaf. On a single emitted tree, the earlier connected children draw in slot order, then the shared path draws, then the last connected child draws. A connected empty quadrant can occupy that last slot. MaterialCraft now orders the raster ranges after evaluating the drawing properties. The ordinary package retains its connections.

Build an FX-Map with nine quadrant subdivisions on a white background with roughness zero and opacity one. Follow child slots 0, 3, 1 to the fork. ### Working precision of Blur inputs

When an equal-sized normalized input feeds Blur and exactly one size depends on a graph parameter, the filter reads the texture at its floating-point destination precision. U8 and U16 inputs to F16 Blur are stored at half precision before the first pass. F32 Blur retains the normalized values and samples them as floats. The second pass reads the stored horizontal result. For fractional taps, the sampler precision affects the result even with identical source texels.

Use the 16² U8 field of 58 with four changed neighbors from the Sharpen comparison. Have the input, Blur, both or neither read an exposed .375 and return (0,0) as the relative size offset. The fixed and both-reader settings agree. The two single-reader settings also agree. Each cell gives the value read from the reference output on one and eight processors. [Procedural field and size functions](#half-precision-inputs-to-sharpen)

| Intensity · destination | Pixel | Fixed or both sizes | One size reads the parameter |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| 24 · F16 | (7,8) | .185546875 | .1854248046875 |
| 32 · F16 | (6,7) | .2100830078125 | .2099609375 |
| 32 · F32 | (6,5) | `0x3e673a97` | `0x3e673a99` |

At intensity 32 with one size reading the parameter, filtering the already stored half pixels with F32 weights gives 251/256, maximum .0001220703125. Sampling them at F16 gives 256/256. For the F32 destination, the previous normalized sampler gave 213/256, maximum 9.9837779999e−7. Sampling the same normalized values at F32 gives 256/256.

### Keeping an explicit file link when the configured library changes

Ordinary Save keeps an explicit file reference tied to the file it resolved when the caller was opened. Previously, a caller outside the configured library could acquire a catalog alias when its explicitly linked package matched bundled bytes. Changing the configured library then redirected that saved caller to a different file.

Use the four configured Waveform v2 callers with U8, U16, F16 and F32 outputs. Put two copies of the hash package in separate library directories. Keep the first original. In the second, set the result of the two-component hash function to .375. Keep the general math dependency equal in both. Open the callers outside either library with the first library configured and use ordinary Save. For each size try the relative filename pointing into the first directory and an explicitly authored catalog alias. Verify both linked file hashes before and after each caller save. Then save the first hash package at its own path so the reference compiler can read its version. Keep the saved callers fixed and reopen them with each directory configured. [Caller dimensions, settings and original function edit](#editing-the-linked-function-with-a-waveform-caller-open)

With the second library configured, the previous relative-file saves matched **8,410/8,448** pixels of the original-function captures. All 38 differences were in the 16² U16 case at seed 725048, with a maximum of 65,535 levels. The corrected relative-file saves match **8,448/8,448** under either library, maximum zero. The four explicit catalog callers follow the configured library, matching all 8,448 original-function pixels with the first library and all 8,448 edited-function pixels with the second. Each comparison uses the raw words from both one and eight reference processors. A fresh open of the four corrected relative-file saves in the reference app also reproduced **8,448/8,448** original pixels at each processor count.

The regression starts with an explicit disk reference to a bundled grayscale switch. It checks the resolved file after saving and reopening the caller and the catalog alias in a separate portable copy. Its in-place assertion failed on the previous engine. The older detached-package compiler behavior is recorded separately. [Reference app’s ordinary Save](#ordinary-save-in-the-reference-app-with-the-same-live-dependencies)

#### Keeping catalog links when saving a caller inside its library

An ordinary Save previously converted an explicit catalog link to a relative filename when the caller was inside the selected library. A later change of library still picked the old function. The in-place writer now preserves the authored choice for both graph instances and function calls.

Create two library directories with the same general math package. Put the original hash function in the first and set its two-component hash result to .375 in the second. Under the first directory, create a child folder for callers. Use the four configured Waveform v2 inputs from the preceding comparison. With the first library selected, save each caller at its existing path. Keep all four external package files fixed and verify their hashes. Reopen all eight saved callers with each library selected. ### Saving a catalog dependency while its callers stay open

A caller could keep an old graph or function after another tab saved the physical file selected by its catalog link. The open session refreshed the disk filename and retained an earlier snapshot under the catalog URI. Ordinary Save now refreshes the catalog entries for that file. It reads nested references relative to each catalog entry. An explicit dependency supplied by a project retains its own value.

Keep one caller open and export its original output. Open the linked package by its physical filename in a second tab. For Points Preview, add a U8 grayscale Uniform at .375 to the linked graph, connect it to the output and save. For Waveform v2, set the linked two-component hash function’s result to .375 and save. Return to the caller tab and export. Undo the connection or function edit, save the dependency a second time and export from the still-open caller. Verify the caller’s file hash through the three exports. Repeat with a relative filename and a catalog URI in each configured caller. [Four Points Preview views and font placement](#points-preview-graph-links-after-switching-the-configured-library) · [Four Waveform sizes, seeds and storage formats](#saving-older-linked-packages-at-their-existing-paths)

### Half-precision inputs to Sharpen

Sharpen reads equal-sized normalized integer inputs at half precision when it writes F16 and exactly one of the two sizes depends on a graph parameter. The shared evaluator now applies that conversion before the four-neighbor filter. The 55 grayscale and RGBA probes improved from **23,181/30,976** to **30,976/30,976** pixels on both reference processor counts. The maximum component error fell from .001953125 to zero.

For a minimal case, fill a 16² U8 input with 58. Store 5 at (7,8), 78 at (9,8), 31 at (8,7) and 42 at (8,9). Use intensity 1 and an F16 destination. The four images now match all 1,024 pixels. For the larger series use the same procedural fields, sizes and seeds as the Levels comparison, intensity 1 for gray and .4375 for color. Include U8, U16, F16 and F32 sources, and check the F32 output control. Six configured ordinary saves reproduce all 3,584 pixels. The 130 repeated Levels controls retain 56,320/56,320. Warp now uses the resolved pixel ratio when measuring displacement. With a gradient the same size as the output, its slope is the current texel minus the adjacent texel on that axis. At intensity one, multiply the slope by the squared axis length divided by 256 to get the displacement in stretched output pixels. The square-pixel setting uses the shorter axis as its length for both directions. For example, with a step of .5 horizontally and .25 vertically at the center of a 32 × 16 image, the center samples the source 2 pixels right and .25 pixels down in stretched mode. With square pixels it samples .5 pixels right and .25 down.

For independent controls, use X and Y coordinate ramps with a single-pixel impulse or a two-axis step gradient. ### Driven seeds in pattern nodes

A pattern node's Random Seed expression now uses the same scalar storage arithmetic as a graph or filter seed. It still reads the incoming pattern stream and the variables available to the node. A driven float-to-integer conversion returns the F32 word of the floored value. A driven scalar sum adds the two 32-bit words. Rounding an intermediate signaling NaN sets its quiet bit and retains its sign and payload.

Use a single additive square with Random(1) luminosity over .125 gray. Drive its parent Iterate's seed with a float converted to an integer, a sum of two floats converted afterward, the sum of two individually converted floats, a product converted afterward, and a converted literal −1.5. Repeat the single-float cast on a Switch and a Quadrant. On a Quadrant also convert ten times the Y component of `$pos`. ### Compile-time conditions before a shared pattern draw

A quadrant can use the same random value in an optional assignment and in a later calculation. With a compile-time condition, the discarded arm consumes no draws. In the test below, a condition that reads an exposed variable yields different pixels even when it selects the same arm as a constant condition. An unwired argument of a called function behaves as a constant in this comparison. MaterialCraft now keeps this distinction when compiling pattern branches.

Use a full-coverage additive square over black at 16² F32. Give its opacity function three separate Random(1) nodes A, T and E. Form L = A + (inner ? T : .3125). In the first input of a Sequence, store S = outer ? L : .1875. In the second, return (E × .5 + L × .25) + S × .125. Render both inner switch values at seeds 0, 113 and 137. Keep the pattern seed offset at its default. For the direct and called forms of T use Random(1) and a zero-argument function returning that draw. For the packed form, pack A and the inner result as Float2, then sum X and Y.

| Folded condition on a direct or called draw | 12 | 1,536/3,072 | 0.143974781 | 3,072/3,072 | 0 |
| Reversed literal, negation and constant comparison | 18 | 0/4,608 | 0.143974781 | 4,608/4,608 | 0 |
| Literal wire, open argument and constant-returning call | 18 | 0/4,608 | 0.143974781 | 4,608/4,608 | 0 |
| Exposed or partly exposed condition | 24 | 3,072/6,144 | 0.151002526 | 3,072/6,144 | 0.151002526 |
| Nested exposed conditions | 48 | 7,680/12,288 | 0.151002526 | 7,680/12,288 | 0.151002526 |

For the fixed conditions, use literal false, swap arms with literal true, negate literal true, or compare .25 > .5. In a called function test its scalar outer argument with > .5 and pass literal zero, leave it open at its zero default, or wire a function returning literal zero. For exposed controls use a public outer value, or AND it with false in each operand order. Exercise both exposed switches in the direct, called and packed forms. ### Storing computed vectors in a quadrant function

A quadrant that stores a computed vector evaluates the operands for its first component before it draws the operands for the second. MaterialCraft now uses that order for stored sums, products, scalar multiples and interpolations. A scalar shared by two components consumes one draw.

Use one full-coverage additive square over black at 16 × 16 F32 and graph seeds 0, 113 and 137. In its opacity function, pack independent Random(1) draws into vectors A and B. Store the result, then return one component of the stored value per render. For widths two, three and four, add A and B, multiply them component by component, scale A by another random draw and interpolate from A to B by .375. Repeat the product after connecting the first component of A to the last component of B. For width two also choose between the two vectors with a condition, then read the selected component. Compare the original on one and eight reference processors and the one-processor reopen of an ordinary MaterialCraft save.

| Vector width | Settings | Previous exact pixels | Previous maximum F32 error | Current exact pixels | Current maximum F32 error |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 36 | 2,304/9,216 | 0.302005053 | 9,216/9,216 | 0 |
| 3 | 45 | 0/11,520 | 0.843028545 | 11,520/11,520 | 0 |
| 4 | 60 | 0/15,360 | 0.71621437 | 15,360/15,360 | 0 |

Each of the three routes matched **36,096/36,096** raw F32 pixels, up from 2,304. Both local renders also agreed in every setting. The three- and four-component interpolation results uniquely fit successive draws for (A₁,B₁), then (A₂,B₂), continuing through the final component. For example, at seed 113 the first two stored components were .496003091 and .551222920. A regression reads both components of five assignments at each of the three stamp seeds.

Pixel Processor product rounding uses the consumers in the original expression. Six size and storage settings for each of 16 independent returned-vector expressions matched **282,624/282,624** pixels, maximum zero, with this fix and at `67ee598`. Use 16² F32 at seed 47, 64² U8, U16, F16 and F32 at seed 223, and 32² F32 at seed 449. The regression for independently returned product components also passed.

The 221 grayscale Tile Generator settings and 175 settings from 35 other qualified roots matched **1,350,656/1,350,656** archived pixels, maximum zero. All 90 earlier pure-function settings stayed exact. Each root in `pattern_splatter_circular.sbs` still matched 13/54 whole settings on one processor, on eight and after saving. [Pure-function expressions](#shared-draws-and-channel-selection-across-pure-pattern-calls) · [Circular geometry and per-format errors](#circular-splatter-geometry-and-the-order-of-random-draws)

### Shared draws and channel selection across pure pattern calls

A quadrant expression can assign a value, call a function and later reuse a draw from a conditional arm. When each called function computes only from its declared arguments and constants, MaterialCraft now preserves the shared draw's position and evaluates only the selected channel of a packed value. The check follows nested calls. A call that draws a random value, samples an image, writes a variable or reads an undeclared name can observe evaluation order.

Start with one ring and one stamp from the [circular geometry control](#circular-splatter-geometry-and-the-order-of-random-draws). Use a full-coverage additive square over black at 16 × 16 F32, offsets (0,0), size (1,1), and seeds 0, 113 and 137. In the opacity graph let A and B be independent Random(1) nodes. Choose A or B by comparing an exposed float of 0 or 1 with .5, assign the result to a named float and return that result plus A/4 plus π/8. Supply π through a constant-returning function. At seed 113 the F32 words for false and true are `3fa910f3` and `3f3da6cd`. Repeat with a literal in place of the call, with and without the assignment, and with another read of the assigned value added to the result.

| F32 controls | Settings | Exact pixels before | Maximum error before | Exact pixels after | Maximum error after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Shared draw, assignment, constant call and controls | 30 | 6,144/7,680 | 1.015005827 | 7,680/7,680 | 0 |
| One or two calls computing from a declared argument | 12 | 1,536/3,072 | .435002476 | 3,072/3,072 | 0 |
| Selecting channels of packed draws or their product | 12 | 0/3,072 | .578230530 | 3,072/3,072 | 0 |
| Direct draws shared across two conditions and independent controls | 36 | 6,912/9,216 | .578230530 | 9,216/9,216 | 0 |

For the argument cases, replace π/8 with a function that returns one eighth of its scalar input. Supply the switch as 0 or 1, directly or through an enclosing function. For the channel cases pack (A,B), select X or Y and store it, then add one quarter of a fresh draw and a function returning .125. Repeat with the X component of (A,B) × (C,D), and with its Y component also added at the end. For the two-condition cases store the first choice between A and B, then add one quarter of a second choice between A and C. Exercise all four switch combinations. Repeat with the first arms reversed and with the second condition using only independent draws. Supply the first switch divided by eight through a function.

Both reference processor counts and the reference reopen of ordinary MaterialCraft saves matched **23,040/23,040** pixels in these 90 settings. The original and reopened MaterialCraft buffers also agreed. In the separate two-condition control where the shared draw happens inside a called function, only 1,536/3,072 pixels matched. When assigning an entire pairwise vector product, sum or interpolation before reading the result, each operation matched 0/1,536 pixels. At seed 113, interpolating (A,B) toward (C,D) by .375 gave (.496003091, .551222920) in the reference. Across all three seeds this matches drawing A, C, B, D.

Grayscale Tile Generator retained **757,504/757,504** pixels in its 221 established settings. One or more archived renders of each of the 15 other qualified roots whose quadrant expressions combine assignments, calls and conditional or channel selection matched **227,840/227,840** pixels in 71 settings, maximum zero. The two circular splatter roots retained the same per-format counts and maxima in all 54 settings each on one processor, on eight and after saving. Both remain in progress. After evaluating opacity, increment the counter and use the requested published scalar as the opacity of an additive square of size (.025,.025). Place successive squares at distinct pixel centers starting at (0,0) in a black, untiled 32² F32 field. The independent control has 12 draws and the one-ring, one-pattern control has one. In the latter, the initial angle 3.103569269 and initial radius .331919193 match. MaterialCraft then publishes radius .277020574 and rotation .457172245, where the reference gives .281947523 and .538937986. Pattern size and tint match.

The two seeds 113 and 137 match 49,152/49,152 F32 pixels on both processor counts and on reopen, maximum zero. At seed 113 the second, sixth and seventh samples are .858505130, .288028121 and .560580373. With only radius variation enabled, MaterialCraft uses sample seven. Sample two reproduces the recorded radius. With only rotation variation enabled, MaterialCraft uses sample six. Sample seven reproduces the recorded rotation. These indices reproduce every observed scalar word at seeds 0, 113, 137, 12071 and 68119. For radius use `r + (r * (r * u) − r) * .15` with r = .35 and unit draw u. For rotation use the starting angle of three quarters of a turn, interpolate in radians toward `2πu − π` by .3, then divide by 2π. Round each operation to F32. Both roots remain in progress.

### Individual paraboloids and additive order in Noise BNW Spots 3 v2

At 64 × 64 F32 and seed 411585, fifteen desktop readbacks agreed with one another and differed from MaterialCraft at three pixels. Record the background and nonzero additive draws there in MaterialCraft traversal order. Each pixel receives eleven paraboloids at depths six through nine. The diagnostic cook reproduces the complete checked release buffer. [Root parameters and full-image comparisons](#seeded-quadrant-properties-with-a-live-tint-multiplier)

To isolate a draw, use a zero background, the same render and tiling intervals and a single additive paraboloid. Set its branch offset to (−.5, −.5). Supply its absolute center, two dimensions and rotation as exposed floats. Set roughness to zero and global opacity to one. Supply its observed scalar tint multiplied in F32 by its depth opacity. On one processor, on eight and after an ordinary SBS save, all 33 individual images match **135,168/135,168 F32 pixels**, maximum zero. At the three selected pixels every individual contribution also equals its corresponding value in the full MaterialCraft render.

For the sum controls, restore the two upstream maps as the background. Connect one drawing Quadrant to the repeated branch of an eleven-count Iterate. Use the repetition number to select each recorded center, dimensions, rotation and tint. Run each group in traversal order, reversed and in the third order shown below. Number the draws 0 through 10 in traversal order. All nine complete images match **36,864/36,864 F32 pixels**, maximum zero on each processor count and ordinary reopen. The forward sum gives the full MaterialCraft value at each selected pixel. Both other orders give the observed full reference word.

| (33, 41) | `0x3f13a394` | `0x3f0d59a0` | `0x3f0d59a1` | 1, 6, 8, 3, 5, 10, 7, 4, 2, 9, 0 |

### Seeded quadrant properties with a live tint multiplier

A grayscale quadrant can set a two-component frame offset and then choose between a seeded scalar and that same scalar multiplied by a live gain. MaterialCraft now reuses the seed-dependent draw properties for a repeated seed, node, depth and selected branch. It reapplies the current gain and publishes the offset in its original drawing scope before visiting children. The other computed fields must depend only on the seed, depth and fixed inputs. A direct read must connect the assigned offset to the frame. Each draw retains its original position in the traversal.

For an independent control, connect four or seven outer iterations to an inner Iterate with seed inheritance disabled. In the count expression publish the outer number and a gain of (1 + number) × .25 or × .125, then return two. Connect a .625 × .375 additive square to the repeated branch. Set an offset from two Rand(.25) draws, then return .0625 + Rand(.125), scaled by the gain when the outer number exceeds 1.5. Use that offset for the square and its negative for four .375 × .25 children at .125 luminosity. Use the [three sizes, seeds and four formats from the initial-branch controls](#the-incoming-seed-on-the-initial-branch-of-an-iterate). All 24 originals match 10,240/10,240 pixels on both processor counts. The 24 ordinary saves also match 10,240/10,240. Maximum error is zero. A bounded regression compares the direct offset with an equivalent computed offset and checks a descendant reading the published value.

### A complete quadrant tree with one physical copy per draw

A single nine-level tree keeps the same submission order when a larger tiled window contains each draw once. The earlier evaluator used the window coordinates to select this order. It now also checks how many physical copies the draws produced in the common render and tiling region. A retained or discarded drawing stamp contributes at least one copy to this count.

In the [two square Noise Dirt 5 comparisons](#shared-branch-expressions-and-all-sixty-noise-dirt-5-renders), expose the FX-Map alongside Levels and set the FX-Map output to F32. Enumerating the orders of those same contributions reaches every differing reference word, including all 68 and 70 differences at 32 × 32 and all 263 and 282 at 64 × 64. The two tabulated coordinates receive six and three contributions. These per-pixel results leave the shared submission order unresolved.

Three drawing quadrants use the same branch offset and tint at successive depths. For grayscale analytic shapes whose only computed drawing properties are a branch offset and an optional tint, the evaluator can reuse their values by seed when both expressions are independent of position, depth, iteration and writable variables. The stamp uses the current depth and extent on every visit. An invisible parent of terminal draws can consume one previous skipped evaluation and one unit from the bounded cache allowance. Its children still run in their original order.

The 128 × 32 U16 control visits 12,583,070 nodes. In a diagnostic MaterialCraft build with room to finish, using separate node and depth keys required 9,038,245 full property evaluations. Starting reuse before the first filled batch and sharing equivalent branch expressions gave 8,122,984 hits and 4,460,086 full evaluations. Both complete buffers have the same raw hash. The latter fits within the existing 5,242,880 full-evaluation limit. A version that kept separate keys for each node and depth still reached that limit.

A normal save gives the three expressions fresh function-node IDs. In a control made from that save, point the three quadrants to the same parameter data record. Keep every expression and connection. The intermediate renderer that keyed on the original IDs now produces the original U16 hash and matches 4,095/4,096 · 3 on one processor. The corrected renderer compares function wiring with relative node IDs for its cache key. Its regression also distinguishes a subtraction whose operands are exchanged.

### Filtering a resized pattern background on each axis

An FX-Map can draw over a clamped, filtered background sample before that sample is rounded to the working texture format. This occurs for a single resize step when the source and receiver sizes are both fixed or both parameter-controlled. Check the connected source's tiling on each axis that grows. If any growing axis repeats, the background is first filtered and stored using the receiver's tiling. A reduction can take the direct path even if its axis repeats. A longer resize or a change between fixed and parameter-controlled sizing keeps the intermediate storage.

### Deferring two tiled subtrees until a quadrant batch fills

When two tiled FX-Map trees share a batch, an earlier split can fall in the preceding 64-parent subtree. A later pair of subtrees resumes at a different position if it cannot fill the receiving batch. This occurs with additive procedural shapes and connected image stamps. The shared evaluator uses the number of physical copies submitted by each subtree.

For an independent test, start a grayscale quadrant graph on white. Let outer iterations 0 and 5 each enter the same complete nine-level tree. Draw original white images or squares at depths 7, 8 and 9 with additive blending. Map pairs of depth-seven parents onto a common interior pixel, with gains −1 and 2⁻²⁵. Swap both gains and repeat the comparisons with adjacent parent pairs offset by one. The two possible results distinguish their compositing order. Hold other draws away from the readout. Move a selected terminal draw from (.875,.875) to (0,.875) to add one tile copy without touching the readout. In the regression, moving the first tree's eight-by-eight corner of terminal draws changes the order of parents 1,955 and 3,868. With no extra copies the readout is 2⁻²⁵ and with 64 it is zero.

To reproduce the panel with more tile copies, distribute a requested number of extra draws among 32,768 depth-seven parents. Store each parent's count in the lower half of an original 256² RGBA field, with one 128-wide bank per tree. At depth nine, move the first requested number of leaves in the parent's four-by-four region across the tile edge, in row-major order. The upper half of the field carries the independent signed readout pairs. Use PCG64 seed 172349. For each candidate draw 64 standard normal values, exponentiate, repeat each weight for 512 consecutive parents in traversal order, and normalize the weights to sum to one. Draw the extra-copy total uniformly from integers 1,100 through 3,599, then select parents with replacement using those weights. Keep candidates 48, 49, 53 and 56. Continue the same random stream with totals 30 through 439 and keep the next four candidates. Each parent in a tree uses the seven interleaved X and Y bits of its traversal index to locate its texel. Across four fields with 37, 253, 240 and 296 extra copies and four with 2,365, 2,135, 2,389 and 2,516, all 524,272 signed comparisons agree with the physical order. Two readout frames on each of four independent fields reproduce 524,288/524,288 F32 pixels on the release build, and 524,288/524,288 after an ordinary save. Maximum error is zero on both routes. More heavily wrapped first-tree controls can cross another subtree boundary and use the existing fallback.

To isolate the 64 × 128 difference, retain the original outer iteration and the assignments in its switch. Gate the drawing branch on iteration 0 and then on iteration 5. Each isolated tree matches all 8,192 F32 pixels. Chain the two gated nodes with an F32 background connection. Each chain matches its corresponding reference chain at all 8,192 pixels. The forward chain matches 8,187 pixels of the original combined reference and the reverse matches 8,173. Three of the five forward-chain differences lie in pixels touched only by the second tree.

For an independent order measurement, repeat a complete four-way quadrant tree through depth nine twice. Use additive grayscale on a white F32 background with both tiling axes off. Keep depths seven, eight and nine active and use a fixed connected white image for each draw. Assign each depth-seven parent a procedural address from its quadrant position and the outer iterator. At each readout pixel overlap exactly two selected parents with gains −1 and 2⁻²⁵. Other stamps draw away from the readouts. Swap the gains to check the opposite sign. Compare adjacent pairs once from the first parent and once from the second so that each parent is drawn only once per image. One tree retains all 32,766 signed comparisons of its earlier order. Two joined trees differ at 30 adjacent boundaries from the concatenated single-tree orders.

On two trees, recover the order from independent pairs of fixed-image parents, then use analytic squares for the final check. All 32,767 adjacent pairs match in both sign directions. The measured order has 103 consecutive parent ranges. Its first 30 agree with the single-tree order. A batch of 5,460 draws fits 260 parents with 21 parent and descendant draws apiece. After two runs of 92 and 128 parents the remaining 40 places split the next run. The shared evaluator accounts for missed stamps when locating boundaries and submits the unfinished first-tree draws with the second tree. A single tree flushes its existing order.

A repeated one-processor read of the same procedural field produced a different stored result during initial order recovery. Eleven later reads of the unchanged input agreed. Rechecking every comparison in both sign directions and testing the complete final order with the second shape gave the counts above. On the original 64 × 128 graph, independently measured contributions at 402 pixels predicted every reference value on one processor, including all 130 previous differences. At 56 pixels more than one address fit the isolated measurements. Every admissible assignment at each pixel predicted the same final value. The complete release read then matched all 8,192 pixels.

The normal cook regression uses two outer iterations. ### Carrying unfinished quadrant draws into a third tree

Noise BNW Spots 1 matches 825,139/841,728 pixels on one processor across its 86 established settings, up from 825,023. The eight-processor capture gives 776,698/841,728, down from 776,739. Ordinary saves give 196,228/196,352, up from 196,200. Whole-frame counts are 66/86, 38/86 and 16/19 respectively. Three original F32 frames changed. At 32² seed 113 and 64² seed 194536, agreement with the established single-processor captures rose from 926 to 941/1,024 and from 3,720 to 3,793/4,096. The maximum in each is 2⁻²². The third changed original and its ordinary save rose from 891 to 919/1,024, maximum 2⁻²³. [Preceding measurements and square settings](#completed-quadrant-batches-before-a-later-tree)

The lower and upper quadrant pairs each complete two 5,460-copy batches with draws from the third tree. When both hand off a single sibling, the lower pair first takes the upper pair's deferred child and the upper pair takes the last pair's deferred child. If three depth-five children remain in the receiver's first incoming depth-three quadrant, the upper pair also takes the third child of the second depth-four quadrant in the adjacent incoming quadrant. At four remaining children that additional subtree stays with other draws. When the lower pair instead hands off two siblings, both pairs carry forward the unfinished pieces from the earlier [two-tree transfers](#final-transfers-between-unfinished-quadrant-groups). The renderer locates those boundaries in the physical tile-copy stream, including copies discarded before rasterization. [Shared renderer](../crates/nodes/src/pattern/underfilled_quadrants/remaining/next_tree.rs)

For an independent boundary check, use three complete eight-level quadrant trees with a connected inactive depth-ten branch. After [the first thirty full batches](#quadrant-batch-order-after-a-sibling-transfer), each group still owns a range of physical copies. If a batch finished inside a transferred child, a further sibling division occurs at that exact copy. The receiver completes its own part of the child and takes a pending child from the upper pair. The next two groups take the following available upper siblings. The third group also takes the lower siblings before the last two. A parent draw between two depth-five subtrees stays with its original group. The final group receives the penultimate lower subtree. The [shared renderer](../crates/nodes/src/pattern/underfilled_quadrants/remaining/transfers.rs) applies this schedule to two complete trees when the lower, upper and last pairs have respectively three or four, five or six, and two through five unvisited depth-five children, the measured transfers line up with subtree boundaries, and each receiving group stays below 5,460 copies.

## 2026-11-25 root comparisons

### Completing partial copy batches above inactive quadrants

Use the [two active drawing levels and the original edge-square field](#which-half-quadrant-completes-the-next-copy-batch). The 64 depth-three quadrants each contain 16 depth-five subtrees. After the first eleven batches fill, two receiving streams can transfer different children of the same pending sibling. Finishing those streams in traversal order changed the sum of overlapping F32 draws. MaterialCraft now splits the pending sibling at its depth-five boundaries and counts each physical tile copy when a receiving stream fills. [Shared traversal](../crates/nodes/src/pattern/tile_runs/inactive_children/completion.rs) · [Regression tests](../crates/nodes/src/pattern/tile_runs/inactive_children/tests.rs)

To vary the incoming work, move draws `50 × 1280 + 2 + 23j` to one tile edge for consecutive j starting at zero. Compare zero, nineteen and twenty additional copies. Independently move forty or seventy draws at `g × 1280 + 1 + 9j` in group g = 24 or 40. At 256² F32 and seed 612671, leave the wrapped squares active. Place consecutive pairs of single-copy draws on separate pixels in two alternating sets so each draw has only one destination per render. Exchange the gains −1 and 2⁻²⁵ to verify the order in both directions. The four fields with 40/0, 0/40, 40/40 and 70/70 extra copies in groups 24/40 matched all **327,376/327,376** adjacent comparisons, maximum readout error zero. The four physical-copy densities taken from the 16² default and seeds 560971, 560983 and 561019 matched all 80,688, 80,690, 80,660 and 80,568 adjacent comparisons respectively.

The stream starting in groups 60–61 can also fill a 5,460-copy batch. With twenty extra copies in group 50, add e copies to groups 60–61 by visiting draw `60 × 1280 + (211j + 17) mod 2560`. Move the first ⌊e/3⌋ squares to a corner and the next e mod 3 squares to one edge. At e = 2,580 the stream fills after the eleventh earlier batch. At 2,740 it fills after the seventh and at 2,900 after the third. Fifteen fields at and around the boundaries matched **1,214,619/1,214,619** adjacent comparisons in both gain directions. Sixteen further fields independently varied the work arriving from groups 24 and 40. Of their 1,294,534 adjacent comparisons, 1,294,516 agreed in both directions. In the remaining 18 the two gain directions returned different orders. A full stream involving groups 62–63 and 48–49 can redistribute more children and remains open.

### Which half-quadrant completes the next copy batch

Use the [two active drawing levels above two inactive levels](#tile-copies-in-the-last-two-active-quadrant-levels). At 128² F32 and seed 91771, number the 81,920 active draws in traversal order and divide them into 64 groups of 1,280. The incoming pairs start in groups 50, 58 and 54 and enter groups 16, 0 and 32 respectively. To add one physical copy, move a single square to the horizontal tile edge. Keep the signed markers on interior squares and repeat each comparison with the gains exchanged.

In the first incoming pair, move draw `50 × 1280 + 2 + 23j` for consecutive j starting at zero. With 19 edge draws, the first receiver transfers a depth-five sibling and the remainder of groups 24–31 submits ahead of the remainder of groups 40–47. With 20 edge draws, the receiver transfers a depth-four sibling and the two remainders exchange places. In both cases each remainder starts after its first 5,460 copies and takes enough copies from groups 52–53 or 56–57 to complete the next batch. Five disjoint marker pairs change order at that single-copy boundary. [Measured pairs and regression tests](../crates/nodes/src/pattern/tile_runs/inactive_children/tests.rs)

Vary all three incoming pairs independently over zero and twenty additional copies. Then move 19, 20 or 21 draws in just one pair, in the receiving half or after the first cut. The order calculated from the first transfer matched 12,240/12,240 signed comparisons across eighteen fields, maximum F32 readout error zero. Independently moving 39, 40 or 41 draws in the later halves or their partners produced 5,440/5,440 agreements. For a second spacing, move the second child at offset `2 + 5j` in group 50. Eleven fields with 40 through 320 extra copies matched another 7,480/7,480 comparisons. At 360, 400, 450 and 490 extra copies the first transfer was larger. Neither order accounted for all 680 comparisons on any of those four fields.

After those batches, the first receiving half submits its tail, followed by the siblings deferred in the middle receiver and the last receiver's tail. This continuation also depends on whether the third leading half can fill another batch with its transferred siblings. Seven separate underfilled fields gave 660/660 signed agreements apiece around these boundaries. In a field with twenty edge squares per group, reversing the gains changed 79/660 inferred comparisons. The remaining 581 agreed. The denser fields that can fill this third batch retain the earlier traversal. [Shared copy calculation](../crates/nodes/src/pattern/tile_runs/inactive_children.rs)

For an independent whole-image check, use the nine marker pairs in the two regression tests above. Split pairs sharing a draw between renders. Use zero, nineteen and twenty edge draws, both gain directions and the [four sizes, seeds and formats](#tile-copies-in-the-last-two-active-quadrant-levels). The 48 original frames match 786,432/786,432 pixels and their 48 ordinary saves also match 786,432/786,432, maximum zero. Each series previously matched 786,396 pixels with maximum error 2⁻²⁵.

The earlier four-format procedural series with inactive descendants now matches 131,070/131,072 pixels on originals and again on ordinary saves, up from 131,066 on each. Each remaining difference is one F32 pixel of magnitude 2⁻²⁵ in one of the two gain directions. The corresponding series terminating at the last drawing level retained 131,072/131,072 on each pass, maximum zero.

At 16² and seed zero the final tree draws 16,384 parents at depth seven and four children per parent at depth eight. The 80,689 interior, 1,227 edge and four corner draws generate 83,159 physical tile copies. To observe their order, make an independent graph with a single outer iteration and switch, four children per quadrant, a single iteration on the way to depth seven, and unselected branches reaching depth ten. Use additive squares on white. Enable tiling on both axes. Place unmarked squares inside the tile, on the left edge or at the lower-left corner for one, two or four copies. Give two single-copy squares gains −1 and 2⁻²⁵ and place them on the same pixel. Repeat with the gains exchanged. The two reads identify which square drew first.

In the 16² root, 196 pixels have the same stored sum for every order of their contributors. The other 60 pixels involve 404 distinct single-copy pairs. Measure all 404 pairs on the independent graph in fourteen 128² F32 renders. Applying these comparisons to MaterialCraft's own background and individual draw contributions reproduces 256/256 original and 256/256 reopened pixels on one processor, maximum zero. The same replay matches 228/256 pixels on the seven-processor capture, maximum 1.19209290e−7. Removing the interior and outer routes and stopping the tree at depth eight reverses nine of the 38 relationships required by the original and reopened pixels. Keeping the inactive descendants alone preserves all 38 on this field.

The first probe used horizontal tiling, giving the four corner draws two copies each. Repeating all fourteen renders with both axes enabled gives the same 404/404 signed comparisons and the same three raw-pixel replay scores.

The renderer before the shared tile-copy correction differs on the F32 settings above. The inventory remains 480/546. [Whole graph across 87 settings and 19 ordinary saves](#copy-batches-from-the-final-quadrant-pair-and-the-following-group)

### The next full batch in an eight-level quadrant tree

In a complete additive tree, start with the [six leading batches](#leading-copy-batches-in-complete-quadrant-trees) and the [5,460-copy batch in the last root quadrant](#a-full-copy-batch-in-the-last-root-quadrant). Number depth-two quadrants 0–15 and depth-three subtrees 0–63 in child-slot traversal order. When the seventh batch reaches either of the final two depth-five subtrees in subtree 49, the next full batch begins with quadrant 12, continues through subtrees 50 and 51, and takes the remaining copies from quadrant 4 and its descendants. Physical copies count even when they miss the image. The shared quadrant renderer applies this prefix to trees with a draw at every depth from two through eight and two full batches per depth-two pair. ## 2026-11-24 root comparisons

### Undefined components in a computed quadrant tint

A quadrant can blend a computed tint with one undefined component. In a color square, an undefined red with finite alpha affects red alone. Floating outputs store the undefined channel as `0x7fffffff` in F32 and `0x7fff` in F16. Both integer formats store zero. A grayscale quadrant uses the alpha of a computed color. A square with undefined alpha or undefined scalar luminosity leaves its background visible. The horizontal offset ramp blends at undefined opacity and produces undefined components. [Quadrant property evaluation](../crates/nodes/src/pattern/evaluation.rs) · [Per-channel storage](../crates/nodes/src/pattern/raster.rs) · [Regression cases](../crates/nodes/src/pattern/tests.rs)

To reproduce, connect four child slots of a quadrant to one unit square. Use a color background of (.25, .375, .5, .75), or its grayscale value .375. Subtract a published scalar from itself and divide the resulting zero by itself. In color, place the result in red of (red, .25, .125, .5), replace alpha in (.125, .25, .125, alpha), or use the result as a scalar tint. In gray, use the scalar and both color vectors. Test all six at blend mode 0, then red, alpha and gray scalar at mode 1 and red and gray scalar at mode 2. At mode 0 the color square with undefined red stores (NaN, .5, .5625, .875). Modes 1 and 2 store (NaN, .3125, .3125, .875).

Use the published default .8125 at 16² F32 with seed 40991 and 32 × 16 U16 with seed 41005. Use .3125 at 16² F16 with seed 40998 and 32 × 16 U8 with seed 41012. Save each of the eleven graphs normally in MaterialCraft, reopen it in the reference desktop, and compare the raw channels. For the shape controls, use mode 0 with red, alpha and gray scalar tints. Test a Gaussian and both offset ramps, variation .375, then a connected uniform image with color (.5, .25, .125, .75) or gray .5. Repeat each with subtraction in place of division to supply finite zero.

## 2026-11-23 root comparisons

### Independent writable variables in six-level quadrant trees

In a plain quadrant tree with six subdivision levels, each connected child of the root starts its own writable variable scope. Successive visits within that child retain the value at the declaring depth. With five full levels a counter spans all four root children. The evaluator checks the reachable nodes and terminal depths before starting separate scopes. An active declaration on the root remains available to descendants that only read it. [Scope handling](../crates/nodes/src/pattern/variables.rs) · [Traversal](../crates/nodes/src/pattern/evaluation.rs) · [Five- and six-level regression](../crates/nodes/src/pattern/tests.rs)

Use a full six-level tree, a tree with all four root children followed by five single-child levels, and one with only opposite child slots at every level. For a five-level control, use all four slots throughout. At the leaves, draw a unit square and keep the first visited position in a local float. When the value is zero, write .125 + .5 × (1 + x + sy) / s², where s is the number of cells along an axis and (x,y) is the zero-based cell. Otherwise write the existing value. In the 64² complete tree the first positions have linear indices 0, 32, 2,048 and 2,080. There are four counters even when each root child contains only one leaf.

For two other original fields, add 1/4,096 to a local counter at depth six or depth one in a complete six-level tree. Read the F32 field in a Pixel Processor using nearest sampling. Subtract the first pixel and add .125. For the depth-one field give the leaves a positive gain of 1e−30. Subtracting the first pixel removes an initial offset observed across separate reference renders of uninitialized variables. At 64² the depth-six field records 1,024 increments per root child. For both counter fields and all four first-position fields render s², 2s × s, s × s/2 and s × 2s. Use s = 64 for six levels and 32 for five. Use seed 598241 + 283i + j for size index i and format index j in the table order. Repeat after an ordinary save and reopen.

### Inherited and writable variables across quadrant depths

A quadrant child can read a value assigned by its parent. When the child declares the same name with Set, it opens the last value written at its own quadrant depth. Later writes at that depth can continue from that value across sibling nodes. A sibling that only reads the inherited name still sees the parent’s value. Iterate and Switch keep the current quadrant depth. MaterialCraft now saves and restores the two bindings separately. [Variable evaluator](../crates/nodes/src/pattern/variables.rs) [Traversal regression](../crates/nodes/src/pattern/tests.rs)

Start with an empty root quadrant. Its branch offset assigns .25 to a named variable and returns (0,0). Connect additive squares in all four child slots. In slot order, write .8125 and emit it, read the parent’s value, add .0625 to the child binding and emit it, then perform the same increment again. On black the four F32 quadrant values are (.8125,.25,.875,.9375). Previously the second quadrant also emitted .8125. ### Bounded work for empty terminal quadrants

A quadrant can evaluate its properties, produce no shape and finish with every child disconnected or behind a cached empty switch. After evaluating the properties and resolving the children, the evaluator charges the visit to the existing discard allowance while units remain. An empty terminal quadrant uses an ordinary visit once that allowance runs out. A quadrant with no shape and a live child also uses an ordinary visit. [Evaluator](../crates/nodes/src/pattern/evaluation.rs) [Budget regression](../crates/nodes/src/pattern/tests.rs)

For two subdivisions and three repetitions, render 16², 32 × 16, 16 × 32, 64 × 32 and 64² in U8, U16, F16 and F32. For size index i and format index j in that order, use seed 51271 + 31i + j. The original and its ordinary SBS save each match 29,696/29,696 pixels, maximum 0.

At each size use U16 and F32, with j = 0 and 1 respectively. Previously all eight original and reopened renders reached the visit limit. They now match 1,536/1,536 pixels in each package, maximum 0. With a small test allowance, switching to a live child or requesting additional repetitions still returns the execution-budget error.

### Wide first-level shapes in additive quadrant trees

The first-level shape in a complete eight-level quadrant tree can wrap more than twice on an axis. Counting those copies against the separate first-level batch restores the measured order of draws in the deeper subtrees. The shared renderer uses the stamp's rotated bounds and the graph's render and tiling regions. ### Submission order in underfilled eight-level quadrant trees

In depth-first order starting at zero, move cells 50 and 0 to (.25,.25) and the others to (.75,.75). Give cell 50 gain −1, cell 0 gain 2⁻²⁵ and the others .125. Set the authored square size to (.875,.875). The center of the first mark reads 2⁻²⁵. Traversal order gave zero. In three repetitions with gain −.25, the same mark reads .25 plus three units of 2⁻²⁵. The original and its ordinary SBS save give identical readouts at 32², 64 × 32 and 32 × 64 with seeds 41381, 17 and 42. The three-repeat check improves from 5,048/5,120, maximum 8.94069672e−8, to 5,120/5,120 on each pass.

The shared renderer groups the draws below each depth-two quadrant into its own draw and its four child subtrees. The measured path covers additive analytic shapes with all 64 depth-three subtrees occupied in each repetition and every submission group below that boundary. ### Runtime scalar arithmetic in graph and node seeds

A graph or node can compute its random seed from a caller's parameters. Converting a driven float to a seed preserves the 32-bit representation of its floored value. For example, a width of 16 supplies `0x41800000`. Runtime scalar addition in a seed expression adds the operand words modulo 2³². With .75 and .25 the resulting word is `0x7dc00000`. Subtraction and multiplication in the measured expressions use ordinary float arithmetic. A folded conversion of the constant −1.5 returns the integer −2. The shared evaluator now selects these operations when evaluating a base random seed. [Regression covering both seed properties](../crates/eval/tests/seed_arithmetic.rs)

To reproduce the direct measurement, feed two exposed floats from a parent to a child. Use the first operand, their sum, their difference or their product, followed by a scalar float-to-integer conversion. Apply the result to the graph or to a grayscale F32 Pixel Processor returning Random(1). Compare all 256 stored pixels at 16² for (.75,.25), (1.75,.25), (−.25,.5), (−1.25,−.5), (5.125,1), (16,1), (32,2) and (0,−1). Each seed property matches **8,192/8,192 pixels**, maximum zero. Return the same expressions through a typed Value Processor, an integer instance argument and a float instance argument. Each matches 32/32 typed results, maximum zero.

Nine further graph-seed expressions cover comparisons against zero and one, multiplication before or after addition, absolute value, subtraction after addition, the sum of two converted integers and the folded negative constant. They match 18,432/18,432 F32 pixels on the originals and another 18,432/18,432 after an ordinary save and desktop reopen, maximum zero. Direct size and argument checks at 16² and 32 × 16 match 15,360/15,360. The three dimension conversions that previously matched 0/3,072 now match 3,072/3,072 on both originals and saves. Moving the sum, product and conversion predicates to graph size, node size and node format gives 3,072/3,072, 3,072/3,072 and 6,144/6,144 pixels respectively, maximum zero.

For the whole-root test, instance BNW Spots 1, Clouds 1 or Clouds 2 beneath a child with the computed seed. Use the changed caller from the integer-seed comparison. For each root, try the first operand converted to integer, the converted sum, the converted product, an integer 5 or 0 selected by whether the sum exceeds zero, and the sum of the two converted integers. Render at 16² with seed 0 and (1.75,.25), 64 × 32 with seed 17 and (−1.25,−.5), 32 × 64 with seed 372177 and (5.125,1), and 32² with seed 372421 and (.75,.25). Read the actual U16 output in the desktop with one eligible processor. [Caller settings and seed inheritance](#computed-graph-seeds-on-load-evaluation-and-save)

| Root | Previous exact / total · maximum U16 codes | Corrected original · max | Corrected after ordinary save and reopen · max |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| BNW Spots 1 | 6,657/26,880 · 43,285 | 26,880/26,880 · 0 | 26,880/26,880 · 0 |
| Clouds 1 | 6,657/26,880 · 45,527 | 26,880/26,880 · 0 | 26,880/26,880 · 0 |

A discarded draw leaves the next random value available. A write, a draw used elsewhere or a draw multiplied by zero in the returned expression can still advance the stream. ### Float vector arguments in nested functions

Fixed two-, three- and four-component float arguments now retain literal precision when an instance supplies the child graph's default, a stored vector, or a constant expression. A vector read from an exposed parent parameter retains runtime precision. This uses the graph evaluator's existing distinction between fixed and driven arguments. ### Ordinary SBS saves with verified library dependencies

Opening a library file by its disk path and saving an ordinary SBS outside the library now preserves portable links through nested packages. Before emitting a library alias, the save verifies each reachable package against the bundled bytes and compares its loaded graphs using the same resolved call interfaces. A dependency with a changed file, edited graph, or local resources keeps its disk link.

Open `panorama_position.sbs` from its library folder and use `file.saveCopyAs` into an empty folder. The saved package now refers to `sbs://panorama_shape.sbs`. File hashes before and after each save confirm that all three source files retain their contents. The engine regression also edits a loaded grandchild graph in memory and verifies its parent keeps the disk link on reopen.
